newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may cut federal oil export programmes.
newsitem.headline: Russia may cut federal oil export programmes.

text.p: Russia may slash the number of federal crude oil export programmes under which it requires domestic companies to export oil to help finance various state-sponsored projects, Interfax news agency said on Friday.

It said that out of the scheduled 53.20 million tonnes (around 1.06 million barrels per day) of oil scheduled for delivery abroad in 1996 under the programmes, 25.7 million tonnes of the total could remain undelivered by the end of this year. It gave no reasons for the forecast cut-back.

Under the programmes, a Soviet-era holdover, domestic companies are appointed to buy oil at lower, domestic prices and then to export it to realise profits which are then partially channelled back to the government to finance various industrial and social programmes.
So-called federal oil accounts for about one-third of Russia's total oil exports. Russia exports about one-third of its 6.2 million bpd output outside the former Soviet Union.

Russia's main Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk is often closed in winter due to winter storms, and it was not clear whether scheduled closures in December would affect federal programme export levels.
Russia has said it will export 40.35 million tonnes (807,000 bpd) of oil in 1997 under federal programmes.

Interfax said the Fuel and Energy Ministry had asked the government to cut significantly the number of programmes, which fill government coffers with foreign exchange, and to allow oil producers, not traders, to carry them out.
